newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares boosted by easing political worries.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares boosted by easing political worries.

text.p: Turkish shares jumped nearly three percent in a wave of late buying on Thursday as market concerns about the future of the country's beleaguered Islamist-led coalition faded, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 index rose 2.94 percent or 42 points to end the day at 1,469. Trading volume rose to 11.59 trillion lira ($85.5 million) from 9.95 trillion ($73.6 million) on Wednesday.

"The market rose generally in late trading in reaction buys," said Can Securities dealer Nadir Erturk. "The market has been influenced more by political than economic news and we have been waiting for news from Ankara," Erturk said.
Speculation that the government of Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan was on the verge of collapse drove shares down nearly seven percent in the week to Wednesday's close.

Sentiment revived on Thursday after Erbakan's coalition partner Tansu Ciller signalled she would stand by her Islamist partners despite a row with the military and the resignation of two ministers from her party.
"The DYP is not going to hide behind anyone and take part in action to topple the government," Ciller told a meeting of deputies from her True Path Party.
Her comments, coupled with buying based on first-quarter results from some companies, encouraged a revival of trading interest, brokers said.
"I think purchases are slowly picking up. Share deals made on loans which had stopped for some time resumed. Political tension eased," said brokerage owner Mustafa Yilmaz.
Brokers said they expected the uptrend to meet resistance at the 1,470-point level and some sounded a warning of profit-taking on Friday in view of the limited trading volume.

"Today's sudden rise was not so healthy because of weak volume. If political uncertainty disappears completely, then there will be more liquidity influx," said Ali Incekara from Alternatif Securities.
Other brokers said the underlying trend would remain positive in the coming sessions providing there was no revival of political uncertainty in Ankara.
"We can see that the market has created its own dynamism at these low prices," said Huseyin Istanbullu of Meksa Securities.
"If we do not receive any negative news about the government in the next few days, the market may start buying on expectations that the government will continue," he said.
Turkish opposition efforts to form a secularist alliance against Erbakan faltered earlier this week.

Erbakan on Tuesday challenged his critics to call elections after coming under heavy fire from the secular establishment over his reluctance to implement military-led measures to curb rising Islamist activism.

A wave of optimism about the coalition's ability to kick-start Turkey's stalled privatisation plans and restore balance to the country's shaky finances lifted shares over 60 percent in the first two months of 1997 in a sustained rally.
Confidence in the 10-month-old government's commitment to economic reform has since waned amid political uncertainty.
Erbakan, who earlier announced a balanced budget target for this year, told his party this week that "major difficulties" had emerged in the budget in March.
Bond yields ended Thursday just under one percentage point higher after the Treasury sold only 10 trillion lira of two-year, inflation-indexed bonds at auction.
The Turkish lira eased to 135,590 against the dollar from 135,240 in line with dollar strength against the mark.
